brief: G1/RI-CAM01 §C.1 — measure the longest run of player_occluded frames against the SHIPPED build, both arms, and say whether the automatic fail is cleared.
what_could_not_be_done: THE FULL 0-500 WALK WAS NOT RUN, AND NEITHER WAS THE FULL 181-FRAME WINDOW I ASKED FOR. Measured: sim frames 275..314, 40 frames, DENSE (every frame, no sub-sampling), fast-forwarded to 275 unmeasured. gl.readPixels-class readback is 10-20 s/call on this box; at 320x180 the observed rate was ~50 s/frame/arm, so the canvas was dropped to 160x90, which reached ~15 s/frame/arm and then eased to ~25 s under fleet load. The remaining 141 frames would have been ~50 minutes of unattended running and were not taken. If a longer run exists outside [275,314] this measurement does not see it — but the bar is already broken INSIDE the measured frames by a CLOSED run, so a wider window can only make the number worse, never better.

RI-CAM03 (lock-on framing) NOT JUDGED. Its own Comparison method M1 requires 7 scenarios at frames_locked >= 3600 each (~25,200 locked frames), plus M2's 40-pose pitch grid, M3, and 40 latency trials. That is a full round, not a leftover from a measurement task. The instrument exists (corpus/80-methods/m-cam03-lockon-framing.mjs delegating to tools/camera/cam-probe.mjs --probe lock,pitchlaw,latency and tools/camera/cam-pitch-instrument.mjs --m2); the `onScreen(eid)` harness method the item asks for is NOT in game/src/harness/api.js (grepped: 0 hits). Left named and unstarted.
RI-CAM04 (directional roll clips) IS NOT JUDGEABLE AND THAT IS THE FINDING — see ri_cam04 below. Not a zero against the build; corpus/build debt.

RI-CAM01's declared blind pair (two unlabelled arm_len time series, ours vs one generated from §C's law) was NOT run. CLAUDE.md rule 0e: only the orchestrator can spawn a fresh blind judge; a subagent cannot. This caps RI-CAM01 independently of §C.1.
The occluder at sim 285+ was identified from a 160x90 evidence frame plus geometry, NOT from a high-resolution multi-angle capture. Stated as an inference below, not as a measured fact.
headline: RI-CAM01 §C.1's automatic fail is NOT CLEARED. On the shipped build there is a CLOSED run of 26 consecutive player_occluded frames (sim 285..310) against a bar of <= 6 — over four times the bar, and 0.43 s at 60 Hz, where §C.1's own rationale is that anything past 0.1 s is long enough to hide a roll's i-frame window. The b476b55d sightline fix is real and does what it claims, but it is not the fix for THIS occluder: both arms of the delete-the-fix are byte-identical over the whole window.

the_measurement.bar: RI-CAM01 §C.1: player_occluded[f] = 1 if the character's visible pixel count is < 0.35x its unoccluded count at the same pose (fade forced to 1.0). Longest run <= 6 frames; mean <= 0.03 on a traversal.
the_measurement.why_the_window_is_shorter_than_requested: The walk was advancing at ~25 s/frame/arm with both arms in parallel and was stopped at 40 frames rather than left running unattended for a further ~50 minutes. This is stated because the requested window is what the command line says and the measured window is what the evidence covers, and those are different numbers. It does not weaken the result: the 26-frame run BEGINS AND ENDS inside the measured frames, so it is a closed measurement rather than a truncated lower bound, and a longer window can only add further runs.
the_measurement.sampling: dense — every frame, no sub-sampling (M2b permits every-4th; run-length bars are not safely measurable at stride 4, so dense was used)

arm_fix_on_shipped.longest_run_is_closed: yes — the run begins and ends inside the measured frames, so 26 is a complete measurement of this event, not a window-truncated lower bound
arm_fix_on_shipped.note: The walk was still advancing toward sim 455 when this file was written; rows.jsonl is appended per frame, so the completed manifest can only add runs, never remove this one.

arm_control_delete_the_fix.flag: renderer.province.occlusionSightline = false — the fix's own documented control arm
arm_control_delete_the_fix.result: BYTE-IDENTICAL to the shipped arm on every frame common to both (occludedPx, refPx, armLen, armHit, playerPos all equal).

the_measurement.the_descent_is_real_not_marginal: occludedPx falls monotonically 359 -> 34 px against a reference of ~595-629 px across sim 278..292 (ratio 0.613 -> 0.057). This is a progressive burial, not noise around the threshold.
the_measurement.arm_telemetry_through_the_whole_burial: armLen pinned at 3.993 m (full extension), armHit false on every frame, clipThrough false on every frame. The spring arm never sees the occluder — exactly the verdict's original finding, still true.

what_is_occluding_the_player_and_why_the.inference: The saved evidence frame reports/cam-occlusion-walk/g1-fixon-r3/frames/f0275.png shows the player beneath a RAISED DECK ON POSTS in Lilmoth, with the camera also under the deck looking at the player through vertical posts. The occluder is ARCHITECTURAL, not vegetal.
what_is_occluding_the_player_and_why_the.why_the_fix_cannot_help: Province.updateOcclusion only ever hides canopy InstancedMesh instances registered by _registerOccludable (game/src/world/province.js:1315 registers only b.kind === 'canopy'). A deck post is not a canopy instance and is never a candidate, so the segment test cannot hide it — which is exactly why both arms are byte-identical here.
what_is_occluding_the_player_and_why_the.why_the_spring_arm_cannot_help_either: settlementSolids() (game/src/render/exterior.js:3045) does build box shapes for buildings, and the player is inside Lilmoth so a settlement CollisionCell exists — yet armHit is false on every frame. Posts are thin; a 0.28 m sphere cast passes between them. RI-CAM01 §C.1 names this case in its own opening: the failure 'which a fade-only implementation still suffers whenever the obstruction is thin enough that the sphere cast misses it'. M2b names the route too: cam-walk-boardwalk, 'a stilt-village boardwalk with railings, the thin-geometry case a sphere cast most often misses'.
what_is_occluding_the_player_and_why_the.the_deck_is_not_in_plan_buildings_either: game/data/world/settlements/lilmoth.json puts the settlement origin at [2766.5, 2.77, 5027.5] and carries 33 buildings (18 interior, 5 sealed-with-reason, 10 structure). Through the burial the player sits at roughly offset [0, -1.7] from that origin, and the NEAREST plan building is lilmoth-house-4 at offset [-13.94, 4.6, -1.33] — about 13.9 m away. So the deck overhead is not a plan building, is therefore not turned into a box by settlementSolids(), and is therefore not in the CollisionCell at all.
what_is_occluding_the_player_and_why_the.all_three_of_RI-CAM01s_protections_are_b: Because that deck is in neither the collision set nor the occludable registry, it simultaneously defeats (1) the spring arm — armHit false on every frame; (2) the §D clip_through detector, which is defined against 'the same collision set used in §C' and so reports false even on the frames where the camera is visibly inside the deck slab (see frames/f0295.png); and (3) the near-field occluder fade, which only ever considers canopy instances. This is one absence producing three false negatives, and it is why the frame looks catastrophic while every camera telemetry field reads healthy.
what_is_occluding_the_player_and_why_the.consequence_for_the_next_piece: The remedy that would move this number is NOT more vegetation work. It is either (a) near-field occluder fade extended beyond canopy instances to settlement/deck geometry, or (b) getting the deck geometry into the collision set so the arm and clip_through can both see it. Whoever takes it should not re-derive the vegetation diagnosis — it is correct, landed, and orthogonal to this occluder.

delete_the_fix_discipline_RULES_rule_6.but_the_control_is_NOT_inert_by_construc: Rule 6 demands the teardown be seen to go red. `node tools/visual/occlusion-sightline-check.mjs` run this session at HEAD: Arm A (a tree 7 m from camera, 2 m off the line, 4 m crown draped over it) reports proximity-only = VISIBLE, with-sightline = hidden. So occlusionSightline=false genuinely changes behaviour; it simply has nothing to change on this walk.
delete_the_fix_discipline_RULES_rule_6.and_the_fix_is_live_in_this_region: game/data/world/pois.json puts Lilmoth in region 'western-rootlands'; game/data/world/regions.json gives that region canopy.r = 4.5 m. The old bubble is 5.6 m around the camera and the arm is 3.99 m, so the entire camera-to-player segment sits inside the old bubble; the sightline test can only ever add trees whose crown radius exceeds ~1.06 m. 11 of 13 regions clear that, western-rootlands among them. The fix is therefore NOT structurally inert in Lilmoth — the occluder here is simply not a tree.
delete_the_fix_discipline_RULES_rule_6.honest_statement: Nothing measured in this window can be attributed to b476b55d, in either direction. This measurement neither confirms nor refutes the sightline fix; it shows the fix is not what §C.1 is failing on.

instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_this_.note: tools/camera/cam-occlusion-walk.mjs was inherited built-but-never-run. Five defects, four of them the kind that produce a confident wrong number rather than an error.
instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_this_.1_total_loss_on_interruption: The manifest was written ONLY at completion. The predecessor's two arms died mid-walk and lost 100% of their frames; mine were then killed at elapsed 123 s by what the logs show as an external browser kill ('Target page, context or browser has been closed' in both arms simultaneously — HAZARDS §10's fleet-wide `pkill -f headless_shell` signature) and lost everything again. FIXED: every row is appended to rows.jsonl the moment it is measured, and an interrupted walk now writes a partial manifest with an `aborted` block instead of throwing.
instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_this_.2_the_reference_arm_recorded_an_impossib: refPx is the player's pixel count with all occluders removed — an upper bound by construction. The predecessor's own reports/cam-occlusion-walk/timing-probe-G1/manifest.json contains frame 2 with occludedPx 2568 against refPx 161, ratio 15.95. Cause: the reference is sampled at i=0, before the scene has settled (measured this session at both 161 px and 0 px on identical invocations), then carried forward for REF_EVERY frames. Silently this scores those frames occluded:false — it manufactures a PASS out of a broken reference. FIXED: a warm-up before the first measurement, plus a reference-integrity guard that scores ratio>1.05 or refPx==0 as null rather than false and reports them in a reference_gate block.
instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_this_.3_frame_labels_drifted_from_sim_frames: Row numbers were computed host-side as FROM+i. When a warm-up step was added ahead of the loop, every label silently became 5 frames early — evidence that would no longer line up with the verdict frames it answers. FIXED: the row records sim.frame read from the sim itself.
instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_this_.4_no_liveness_gate: HAZARDS §15 requires per-frame proof that a capture is a picture. FIXED: every measured frame is PNG-encoded from the exact canvas the pixel diff was taken from and run through tools/visual/frame-liveness.mjs metrics/classify. Result on this run: 0 non-LIVE frames.
instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_this_.5_no_motion_proof: HAZARDS §16: no capture in this project had ever photographed a moving player, because setInput was never a harness verb and call() swallowed the failure. Verified the verbs this tool uses DO exist (queueInputs and stepFrames, game/src/harness/api.js:94,98) and that tools/lib/browser.mjs#h() dies loudly on an unknown method rather than swallowing. FIXED: the manifest now carries a motion_proof derived from the walk's own recorded positions. Result: 1.120 m displacement, 21 of 21 frames moved. The walk moved.

method_deviations: Canvas 160x90 rather than the canonical 1920x1080 (HARNESS §6). Reference player pixel counts are ~600 px, ample for a 0.35 ratio test, but this is not the canonical capture size.

PIXEL COUNTING IS A COLOUR DIFF, NOT AN ID BUFFER. §C.1 specifies the ID buffer. RI-MTH04 Appendix A prescribes root.visible toggling (never material mutation, which leaks across actors through shared material instances) and this tool complies. But a colour diff misses player pixels whose rendered colour equals what is behind them. CALIBRATED THIS SESSION: on frames where the player is provably unoccluded the ratio reads p50 = 0.560, not 1.000. The instrument therefore UNDER-reports the visible fraction and is biased TOWARD declaring occlusion. This matters for a marginal result and does not for this one — the frames in the run fall to 34 px of 595 (ratio 0.057), which no plausible recalibration lifts above 0.35.
Per RI-MTH04 Appendix A, root.visible=false also removes the cast shadow, so the figure measured is body-plus-shadow, not body alone.
The measured window's mean_occluded is a WINDOW mean, not the traversal mean §C.1's 0.03 bar is written against. Quoted as a window statistic only.

Appendix A's closing instruction — 'draw the mask at least once' — was carried out. The occluded-arm mask is a clean, correctly placed human silhouette; the reference-arm mask is the same silhouette plus its blob shadow against an emptied scene.

ri_cam04.verified_independently_this_session_not_: grep -rn roll_bin game/ returns 0. Of the nine clip ids RI-CAM04 M1 censuses (roll_f, roll_fr, roll_r, roll_br, roll_b, roll_bl, roll_l, roll_fl, backstep), only `backstep` appears anywhere under game/data/ (5 files); the other eight are absent. corpus/80-methods/m-cam04-locked-movement.mjs is an honest absence-reporter and its claims match my own greps.

next_step: G1 is measured but NOT closed: RI-CAM01 §C.1 still carries its automatic fail, now with a number and a named cause. The next piece is the thin-architecture occluder (deck posts / boardwalk railings in Lilmoth), not vegetation. It needs a builder + a separate critic, and RI-CAM01 additionally cannot pass while its blind pair is unrun (rule 0e, orchestrator-only).
